description.narrative:
Building on the PRMP and other programs, PGEIP will support the GoPb in realizing the long-term goals expressed in Vision 2020, through which the government has committed itself to significantly improving the standard of living of the people of Punjab, especially the poor and vulnerable. The PGEIP will improve the overall functioning of the provincial, district, and municipal governments and the quality of public services. The improvements will take the following forms: (i) greater performance-oriented planning and budgeting; (ii) a more efficient civil service, with adequate incentives and merit-based appointment and career progression; (iii) a funded and well-managed pension system, which increases the confidence of civil servants and the public, and generates fiscal space for high-priority investments in the social sectors; and (iv) greater private sector contribution to growth and facilitation of public-private partnerships.
As reforms in these areas are complex and take time to filter through the bureaucracy, PGEIP will be processed as a program cluster comprising three single-tranche SPs. This modality provides adequate flexibility to meet emerging reform needs and use program conditions genuinely for policy reform, rather than as rigid prescriptions. ADB's Management and Board will also have greater involvement in recommending measures for future operations within a cluster, in a way that is not possible in traditional multiple-tranche operations. Separate reports and recommendations of the President (RRPs) will be prepared for each subprogram. The policy matrix developed thus far for SP1 has indicative actions for SP2 and SP3. In addition, detailed action plans will be developed in combination with policy matrices to guide reforms. In order to ensure that all the six pillars of the Vision 2020 are in place, the GoPb has also sought ADB's support for accelerating the attainment of the MDGs and implementation of provincial-level judicial reforms, in addition to the government efficiency improvements under PGEIP. In line with this request, ADB will also prepare two additional program clusters, namely the PMDGP and PAJP, in an integrated manner along with PGEIP over 2007-2011. The integrated approach and the preliminary details of the PMDGP and PAJP. The integrated approach will improve program coordination, reduce duplication, minimize inconsistency in policy advice and measures, and focus resources for desired outcomes.
The reforms under the three program clusters will accelerate and sustain economic growth, improve the delivery of public services, create more employment opportunities, and reduce poverty.

description.narrative: Greater efficiency in the allocation of scarce resources and greater responsiveness to citizens' needs.

At least 30% of annual pension liability can be met from returns of PPF and GPIF investments by 2014 (Baseline: 0% in 2007) Progress/Status: The pension and general provident fund financing strategy has been revised downwards during PGEIP SP2. In line with the revised financing strategy, Rs6 billion has been transferred in FY2009, and Rs6 billion in FY2010. The transfer due for FY 2011 has been moved to FY2012 Data Source: MTBF; PPF and GPIF reports; ADB review missions Actual value:

The private sector contribution to provincial GDP will have risen to about 40% from the current 30% level by 2014 (Baseline: 30% n 2007) Progress/Status: no data available [tbc] Data Source: Punjab Economic Report; Punjab White Paper; Economic Survey (federal) Actual value:

All officer cadre positions (ie, grade 17 and above) will have come under the new performance-based HRM system by 2014 Progress/Status: The performance-based HRM system has not been pursued Data Source: Civil service perceptions survey; ADB review missions Base year: 2007 Baseline value: N

Budget process fully performance-based, particularly in the social sectors by 2014 Progress/Status: MTBF has been introduced in 7 departments, including health department, higher education department and public health engineering department Data Source: Annual budget document; MTBF; MTDF; multiplpe-cluster survey; ADB review missions Base year: 2007 Baseline value: N
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Civil service efficiency and motivation enhanced Indicator: At least 4 large departments restructured to increase efficiency following functional review and business process reengineering by May 2012 Progress/Status: Functional review, HRM review and BPR review have been undertaken in 3 departments, Punjab Public Service Commission, E&TD and L&DD. Priority reforms identified through the reviews are being supported with TA resources Data Source: GoPb reports; Functional review and business process reengineering reports; ADB review missions Actual value:

Output: Civil service efficiency and motivation enhanced Indicator: At least 8 key departments accounting for about 75% of the Punjab civil service will have embraced performance-based recruitment and career progression by May 2012 Progress/Status: Under SP2, Punjab government has developed a draft result framework for 7 key departments (education, health, water supply and sanitation, irrigation and power, transport, livestock and dairy, and excise and taxation) through a consultative process toward greater accountability for results. Data Source: GoPb reports; ADB review missions Actual value:

Output: Greater private sector participation in economic activity, and a redefined role for the Punjab public sector Indicator: At least 6 to 7 PPP initiatives contracted out in the infrastructure and social sectors by May 2012 Progress/Status: no PPP initiatives were contracted out so far Data Source: Notification from relevant department of relevant PPP agreement Actual value:

Output: Civil service pension system made financially sustainable Indicator: Funded civil service pension accumulations will have increased to at least PRs57 billion in 2011 (Baseline: PRs 12 billion in 2007) Progress/Status: Under SP2, a revised funding strategy was prepared reflecting the changes in fiscal conditions. The revised funding strategy is included in Punjab's Medium Term Fiscal Framework 2009-12. In 2009, the government transferred Rs12 billion to the PPF. The transfer due for FY2011 will be made in FY2012 Data Source: Release letter and bank statement of fund transfers Actual value:

Output: Civil service efficiency and motivation enhanced Indicator: Management and Professional Development Department (MPDD) upgraded to a regionally recognized civil service training institution, from its nascent status in 2007, by May 2012 Progress/Status: MPDD remains a modest training department with approximately 15 staff. MPDD has signed an MOU with the Asian Institute of Technology as part of a twinning arrangement Data Source: GoPb reports; ADB review missions Baseline year: 2007 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2007 Baseline value: N Target year: 2012 Target value: Y

Output: Civil service pension system made financially sustainable Indicator: Pension and GPF system automated and made transparent, with the incidence of errors and fraud significantly reduced by May 2012 Progress/Status: By end 2010, approximately 80-85% of the payroll was automated, 92% of the pension records and about 74% of the historic general provident fund records have been converted from the ledger books Data Source: Government notifications; ADB review missions Baseline year: 2007 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2007 Baseline value: N Target year: 2012 Target value: Y
